strengths: UniAP addresses a useful training-systems problem: jointly selecting pipeline placement and DP/TP/FSDP strategies under communication and memory constraints. The ViT-Huge and Swin-Huge experiments provide direct relevance to computer vision.

Table 2 demonstrates meaningful practical gains. On EnvB, ViT throughput reaches 45.58 samples/s versus 38.74 for the strongest baseline, and Swin reaches 19.08 versus 13.90. UniAP also enables Swin training on EnvA where Galvatron encounters OOM. Search-time improvements remain valuable when throughput ties: EnvA BERT optimization decreases from 6.44 to 0.37 minutes.

The evaluation covers five Transformer models and several hardware configurations. The reported 3.59% mean estimation error and the topology-aware BERT strategy in Appendix E provide useful supporting evidence. Hardware specifications, model dimensions, batch sizes, and solver settings are documented.
weaknesses: The published placement constraints have a material correctness gap. Equations (6a–6c) enforce contiguity within each stage but do not enforce stage order. For a graph u→v, placing u in stage 2 and v in stage 1 satisfies the contiguity and placement constraints, yet Equation (4) charges zero communication because P_u1 P_v2=0. Consequently, the objective can favor an assignment with omitted communication costs. Appendix A proves contiguity, which does not resolve this issue.

The memory-feasibility guarantee is insufficiently supported by the stated model. Algorithm 1 constructs M using micro-batch size b=B/c, and Section 3.2 scales activation memory by the supplied batch size. GPipe without activation checkpointing retains activations across multiple micro-batches before backward execution. The manuscript does not explain where this accumulation enters M or Equation (5); as written, activation memory can be underestimated.

The repeated claims of finding an optimal solution exceed the evidence. Appendix D specifies a 60-second timeout and permits early stopping after 15 seconds with an optimality gap below 4%, but achieved gaps and termination statuses are not reported. Moreover, prediction accuracy on selected strategies does not establish optimality under measured runtime. Section 3.5's fixed-timeout argument bounds a truncated search procedure, not the complexity of obtaining an optimal solution.

The experiments do not isolate the central claim that joint optimization improves upon hierarchical optimization. Figure 7 removes entire parallelism categories rather than comparing joint and hierarchical search with matched cost models and candidate strategies. Hierarchical optimization is not inherently suboptimal; the manuscript needs a precise account of which choices prior methods exclude. Differences in cost estimation and solver threading also complicate attribution of the observed gains specifically to joint optimization.

A correctable but significant reproducibility omission is that Equations (3) and (4) contain fourth-degree products of placement and strategy variables, rather than a directly specified MIQP. An auxiliary-variable reformulation is possible, but none is provided. Together with the unresolved ordering and memory accounting, this prevents verification that the implemented optimization matches the published method. The practical gains are worthwhile, but these central formulation and validation gaps currently favor weak rejection.
